paint-creek.title: Paint Creek
paint-creek.confidence: High for rigs/flies (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub); regs from MDNR
paint-creek.summary: Small, heavily canopied, clear Type 1 trout stream with spooky browns. Roll casts, long light leaders and stealth beat long drifts. Best April-June and September-October; shuts down near 70°F water. Remember: closed Oct 1 to the last Saturday in April; Gunn Rd-Tienken Rd is artificial lures only, 2 trout, 14-in minimum.

dry.boots: Wading sandals or lightweight rubber shoes

flies: Small nymphs, minimal shot or none
Soft hackle wets swung on a tight line
paint-creek.lures: Gunn Rd-Tienken Rd: artificial lures only (no bait), 2 trout/day, 14-in minimum. Elsewhere on Paint Creek (Type 1) bait is allowed - verify in the current Michigan Fishing Guide.
tips: Dry-fly tip from the hub: 'Approach carefully - the fish are spooky in the clear water.' Small dries #14-20 (Sulphurs, BWOs, caddis); floatant.
Nymphing: light nymphing; soft-hackle wets swung on a tight line are often more effective than a full indicator rig.
Guide Kip Lowrie (Morning Sun): fish the sulphur spinner fall or dun hatch; midges, BWO and caddis are the early staples.
safety: Stop fishing for trout when water temperature is above ~68°F (dashboard rule); fish early in warm spells and land fish quickly (general guidance).
Check flow before wading: high or rising water (this dashboard's % of median) means stay on the bank. Wear a belt, use a wading staff in fast/cold water (general guidance).
Paint Creek Trail parallels much of the creek - park at trail lots and respect private property along the banks.
shops: Motor City Anglers (Rochester Hills) - guide service and fly shop; hub lists them as home-water specialists on Paint Creek.

clinton-river.title: Clinton River (and branches)
clinton-river.confidence: High for rigs/flies (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub); steelhead/regs per DNR
clinton-river.summary: Metro Detroit's home water: resident browns in the cold upper reaches above Pontiac, a big spring (Mar-May) and fall steelhead run in the lower river (Yates/Rochester to River Bend). Nymphing is the primary technique year-round; dries (BWO, Sulphur, caddis #14-18) when bugs come off.

dry.boots: Rubber-soled boots (felt banned on some sections)

flies: Steelhead egg patterns (Mar-Apr spring; fall too)
clinton-river.lures: Spin/bait: DNR notes the lower Clinton (River Bend Park, Type 4) works with spinners, spawn bags or wax worms under a bobber; mainly a spring fishery with some fall steelhead. Verify regs.
clinton-river.steelhead: Hub: spring runs Mar-May are best, fish stack in the deeper pools and runs around Rochester and Yates. Egg patterns are 'extremely effective' Mar-Apr; use dark Wooly Buggers and leeches on a 9 ft 6-weight with a 6 ft leader to 1X. Yates Cider Mill sits on prime steelhead water.
tips: Small indicators, steelhead egg patterns in fall/spring; bead-head nymphs 14-18.
Upper river above Pontiac: small streamers and nymphs for resident browns (hub).
Crowded at Yates on steelhead weekends - River Bend Park lets you spread out (DNR).
safety: Stop fishing for trout when water temperature is above ~68°F (dashboard rule); fish early in warm spells and land fish quickly (general guidance).
Check flow before wading: high or rising water (this dashboard's % of median) means stay on the bank. Wear a belt, use a wading staff in fast/cold water (general guidance).
Hub: felt soles are banned on some Clinton sections - use rubber soles.
Urban river: watch for strainers/log jams, slick concrete and sudden rises after rain.
shops: Motor City Anglers (Rochester Hills) guides Clinton steelhead; hub also lists two other SE Michigan outfitters.

huron.title: Huron River (Proud Lake / lower river)
huron.confidence: Medium - no hub page for the Huron; Orvis/Birdtrout + general trout gear
huron.summary: Above Belleville: a stocked-trout fishery in spring (DNR stocks in April) and a Blue Ribbon smallmouth river from the last Saturday in April to late October. Below Belleville Dam to Flat Rock/Rockwood: steelhead, walleye, muskie. Streamers are the preferred tactic.

streamer.line: WF floating (add intermediate/sink-tip in cold high water)

flies: Weighted streamers, low-and-slow retrieve (Orvis winter note)
Hex, White Fly, Isonychia, caddis, hopper and ant dries - bring bass to the surface
huron.lures: Bass: typical smallmouth spin gear and soft plastics work (general). Catch-and-release rules for bass between Mast Rd (Dexter) and Delhi Rd (Orvis) - check current regs.
huron.steelhead: Lower Huron (Belleville Dam to Lake Erie) has steelhead, walleye and muskie (Orvis). Use the steelhead/streamer rig and egg/bead patterns Oct-Jan and Mar-Apr (general; Birdtrout lists fish eggs Oct-Jan and April).
tips: Birdtrout lists winter stones (Jan-Apr), Hendrickson and black caddis (Apr-May) for the Huron watershed.
Spring-stocked trout take eggs, small streamers and nymphs soon after stocking.
safety: Stop fishing for trout when water temperature is above ~68°F (dashboard rule); fish early in warm spells and land fish quickly (general guidance).
Check flow before wading: high or rising water (this dashboard's % of median) means stay on the bank. Wear a belt, use a wading staff in fast/cold water (general guidance).
Dam tailraces (Proud Lake, Belleville) can change flow quickly - check releases before wading.
shops: Orvis lists nearby SE Michigan shops; Motor City Anglers (Rochester Hills) serves the metro area.

au-sable-holy-water.title: Au Sable - Holy Water (Grayling)
au-sable-holy-water.confidence: High for rigs/tips (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub river page); regs from FO-200.25 (Michigan DNR)
au-sable-holy-water.summary: The Holy Water is one of America's premier dry fly rivers. Technical, clear water demands precise presentation and fine tippets. Burton's Landing to Wakeley Bridge is flies-only, no-kill (FO-200); Wakeley to McMasters is artificial lures only; James St to Burton's Landing is Type 2.

dry.line: Double-taper floating (DT4F or DT5F) — less splash on presentation than weight-forward
dry.waders: Chest waders or hip waders in summer
dry.boots: Felt-soled wading boots (rubber with studs acceptable)

nymph.line: Weight-forward floating with a strike indicator setup

euro.line: Level 20lb Maxima or dedicated euro nymph line
euro.leader: Long mono rig (20ft+) with sighter section

streamer.line: WF floating or intermediate sink tip

flies: Hatches the hub lists for this river
tips: The Au Sable's flat pools and educated trout demand the finest tippets. Drop to 7X in low clear conditions. The Hex hatch demands a size 4–6 fly so step up to 3X–4X leader for those nights. (hub)
High-stick nymphing in the braided sections between Stephan and Wakeley bridges. Small bead-head nymphs in size 14–18 match the Au Sable's invertebrate profile. (hub)
Czech and French nymphing techniques work well in the Au Sable's riffles and pocket water. The long rod keeps line off the water in the technical dry fly sections. (hub)
Night streamer fishing during the Hex hatch produces the largest browns of the season. Mouse patterns on a floating line after midnight are a Holy Water tradition. (hub)
Regulations change by reach - check FO-200 / the current Michigan Fishing Guide before you rig up (flies-only reaches ban bait, scent and beads).
safety: Stop fishing for trout when water temperature is above ~68°F (dashboard rule); fish early in warm spells and land fish quickly (general guidance).

au-sable-north-branch.title: Au Sable - North Branch (Lovells)
au-sable-north-branch.confidence: High for rigs/tips (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub river page); regs from FO-200.25 (Michigan DNR)
au-sable-north-branch.summary: The North Branch is intimate fly-only water with wild brook trout. Small stream technique and stealth are more important than gear. North Branch from Sheep Ranch to the confluence is flies-only (FO-200): 2 trout, browns 18-in minimum.

dry.waders: Hip waders or wet wading in summer
dry.boots: Lightweight wading shoes or wading sandals

nymph.boots: Wading sandals or lightweight wading shoes

euro.leader: Short mono rig (12–15ft) adapted for tight brush

flies: Small dry fly box (caddis, BWOs, Hendricksons)
Soft hackle wets and small nymphs size 14–18
Hatches the hub lists for this river
tips: Short-line dapping and roll casts dominate on the brushy North Branch. A shorter rod is essential — backcast room is minimal. Wild brookies are opportunistic so pattern matters less than stealth. (hub)
High-stick nymphing in small pools and runs. Keep the rig simple — one nymph on a short dropper is often more manageable than a full indicator rig in tight quarters. (hub)
Euro nymphing is effective but the long rod can be challenging in brushy sections. Opt for a shorter 10ft rod over an 11-footer on the North Branch. (hub)
Smaller streamers than the main branch. A 2-inch Muddler or small Sculpin swung on a tight line through deep pools can produce surprising brook trout. (hub)
Regulations change by reach - check FO-200 / the current Michigan Fishing Guide before you rig up (flies-only reaches ban bait, scent and beads).

au-sable-south-branch.title: Au Sable - South Branch / Mason Tract
au-sable-south-branch.confidence: High for rigs/tips (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub river page); regs from FO-200.25 (Michigan DNR)
au-sable-south-branch.summary: The South Branch and Mason Tract offer remote, lightly pressured dry fly fishing for wild brown trout. Wading the sandy bottom is easy but the fish are educated. Chase Bridge to Lower High Banks (4.3 mi) is flies-only, no-kill; below that to the confluence is also flies-only, with 2 trout (browns 18-in minimum) kept only last Sat in April - Sep 30 (FO-200; 2026 Fishing Regulations p.44).

dry.waders: Chest waders (hip waders workable in summer)

flies: Hatches the hub lists for this river
tips: The South Branch is a walk-in wilderness fishery. Pack light but bring a map — the Mason Tract has multiple miles of remote water. Afternoon BWO and evening Sulphur hatches are the main events. (hub)
Nymphing the South Branch's deep pools and undercut banks produces well between hatches. Pheasant Tails and Hare's Ears in size 14–16 are reliable. (hub)
Euro nymphing the South Branch's sandy-bottom runs. The lack of current structure makes reading the water critical — focus on seams near logs and undercuts. (hub)
Nighttime streamer fishing in the South Branch's deep pools produces trophy brown trout. Mouse patterns during the Hex hatch window (late June) are highly effective. (hub)
Regulations change by reach - check FO-200 / the current Michigan Fishing Guide before you rig up (flies-only reaches ban bait, scent and beads).

pere-marquette.title: Pere Marquette River (Baldwin)
pere-marquette.confidence: High for rigs/tips (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub river page); regs from FO-200.25 (Michigan DNR)
pere-marquette.summary: The PM is a world-class tailwater — powerful, wide, and demanding. Steelhead and big browns are the primary targets. Drift boat access is the standard approach. M-37 to Gleason's Landing is flies-only with zero trout/salmon kept all year; rules change by reach and date (FO-200).

dry.waders: Chest waders with wading belt (mandatory — powerful current)
dry.boots: Felt-soled boots with studs, or rubber with aggressive studs

streamer.line: WF floating, intermediate, or Type 3 sink tip

flies: Dry fly selection (Hendricksons, Sulphurs, Brown Drakes)
Stonefly nymphs, egg patterns, Copper Johns size 8–14
Large articulated streamers size 2/0–4 (Zoo Cougars, Drunk and Disorderly)
Hatches the hub lists for this river
pere-marquette.steelhead: Steelhead/egg-run notes: swing articulated streamers on a sink tip, nymph stoneflies, eggs and Copper Johns size 8-14 (hub).
tips: Dry fly fishing on the PM peaks in May (Hendrickson) and June (Sulphur, Brown Drake). The river is big — fish the softer edges near the banks and slow inside seams. (hub)

Deep nymphing with heavier rigs than most Michigan rivers. The PM's powerful current requires more weight to get flies down. Swinging soft hackles through runs is highly effective for steelhead. (hub)

Euro nymphing works well on the PM's classic pool-riffle-run structure. Focus on the inside seams of runs and the tail-outs of pools. Heavier tungsten beads needed to reach the bottom in the PM's flows. (hub)

Streamer fishing is the PM's signature — particularly for steelhead on the swing. A sink-tip line and a large intruder-style or Wooly Bugger fished on a downstream swing is the classic PM steelhead approach. (hub)
Regulations change by reach - check FO-200 / the current Michigan Fishing Guide before you rig up (flies-only reaches ban bait, scent and beads).

manistee-upper.title: Upper Manistee River
manistee-upper.confidence: High for rigs/tips (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub river page); regs from FO-200.25 (Michigan DNR)
manistee-upper.summary: The Upper Manistee is classic northern Michigan trout water — intimate, clear, and lightly pressured. Wild browns and brookies on dry flies in wild country. CR 612 to M-72 is artificial lures only; M-72 to the CCC Bridge is flies-only (FO-200). Wild browns/brookies, lightly pressured.
flies: Dry fly selection: Hendricksons, BWOs, Caddis, Hex
Hatches the hub lists for this river
tips: The Upper Manistee fishes like a smaller Au Sable — clear, technical, and rewarding for patient dry fly anglers. Evening hatches from May through July are the prime window. (hub)
High-stick nymphing between pools and in riffles. The upper river has a natural gravel and sand substrate — small naturalistic patterns outperform attractors. (hub)
Euro nymphing is well-suited to the upper Manistee's riffles and runs. Fine tippets and small flies match the river's invertebrate profile. (hub)

Streamers on the upper Manistee are most productive in early spring before the hatches begin, and in fall when brown trout are aggressive pre-spawn. Swing medium-sized Sculpins through deep pools at dusk. (hub)

muskegon-croton.title: Muskegon River below Croton Dam
muskegon-croton.confidence: High for rigs/tips (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub river page); regs from FO-200.25 (Michigan DNR)
muskegon-croton.summary: The Muskegon is a big tailwater below Croton Dam — wide, cold, and powerful. Drift boat fishing is standard. World-class steelhead, brown trout, and Chinook salmon. Tailwater steelhead/brown river, Type 3 from Croton Dam to M-120 (15-in brook/brown minimum; up to 5 rainbows, 1 over 20 in).

dry.boots: Felt-soled with studs or aggressive rubber studs

streamer.line: WF floating, intermediate sink, or full sink (Type 3–6)

flies: Dry fly selection focused on Sulphurs, Hex, Brown Drake
Egg patterns, Stoneflies, Woolly Buggers size 8–12
Large articulated streamers (Zoo Cougar, Circus Peanut, Drunk & Disorderly)
Hatches the hub lists for this river
muskegon-croton.steelhead: Steelhead tailwater - see hub Muskegon page for eggs/streamer/nymph approaches; Aug 1-Nov 15 terminal tackle is restricted (single-point hooks / small trebles on body baits).
tips: Dry fly fishing on the Muskegon is spectacular during the summer hatch season (June–July). The river is wide — look for rising fish in the softer water along grassy banks and shallow inside bends. (hub)
The Muskegon's powerful flow requires heavy nymph rigs. Steelhead nymphing with egg patterns and rubber-leg stoneflies in spring and fall is the primary approach from the bank. (hub)

Euro nymphing on the Muskegon requires heavier flies than most Michigan rivers. Focus on the seams below Croton Dam and the runs between Newaygo and Bridgeton. A 4-weight handles the heavier rigs better than a 3-weight on this water. (hub)

The Muskegon is Michigan's premier streamer fishery. An 8-weight handles the big flies and fall salmon. From a drift boat, cast to the bank and strip through — brown trout stack in the grassy edges. Steelhead respond to a swung streamer on a sink tip in cold water. (hub)

rifle-river.title: Rifle River (Ogemaw Co.)
rifle-river.confidence: High for rigs/tips (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub river page); regs from FO-200.25 (Michigan DNR)
rifle-river.summary: The Rifle River flows through the Rifle River Recreation Area in Ogemaw County — excellent wild trout habitat, relatively uncrowded, and beautiful spring-fed water. Wild brown trout water in the Rifle River Recreation Area; check FO-200 for the Type that applies at your reach (Type 3 listed from Sage Lake Rd to Saginaw Bay).
flies: Medium streamers size 4–8 (Wooly Buggers, small Sculpins)
Hatches the hub lists for this river
tips: The Rifle is an underrated dry fly river. Hex hatches in late June are excellent and uncrowded compared to more famous rivers. Evening Caddis hatches are reliable all summer. (hub)
Nymphing the Rifle's riffles and runs. Smaller, more natural patterns match the river's invertebrate profile — Pheasant Tails and Hare's Ears are reliable. (hub)
Euro nymphing the Rifle's pool-riffle sequences. The river's moderate size and clarity make it ideal for tight-line techniques. (hub)
Fall streamer fishing on the Rifle produces aggressive pre-spawn brown trout. Fish deep pools and undercut banks with a slow, jigging retrieve. (hub)
Regulations change by reach - check FO-200 / the current Michigan Fishing Guide before you rig up (flies-only reaches ban bait, scent and beads).

brookie-creek.title: Tiny brook trout headwater (SE Michigan)
brookie-creek.confidence: Rigs and fly sizes from the Michigan Fly Fishing Hub's wild brook trout page (Fox River, UP); rod/leader lengths shortened for brushy headwaters (* = adapted)
brookie-creek.summary: Tiny, brushy, spring-fed creeks with small wild brook trout. Short rod, short leader, roll casts and dapping; stay low and fish upstream. Type 1 season (last Sat in April - Sep 30) on the designated reach; nearly all banks are private - stay in the road right-of-way unless you have permission.

euro.waders: Hip waders or wet wading (tiny creek)

streamer.waders: Hip waders or wet wading (tiny creek)

tips: Hub (Fox River brook trout): wild brookies are aggressive on any visible adult dry - focus on pool tail-outs morning and evening; small bead-heads #14-16 and soft hackles below.
Roll-cast or dap from the bank; one good first cast per pocket, then move on (general guidance).
Terrestrials (ants, beetles) #14-18 under overhanging grass in July-September (general guidance).
Brook trout spawn in fall - the Type 1 season closes Sep 30; avoid wading over gravel redds Oct-Nov (general guidance).
